subject: Request: carveout on async bulk completion SLA for Acme Analytics
messages:
From: Gabe Morris <gabe@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: dataflow-ops@acmeanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Bulk async SLA needs — completion window flexibility

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited about Redwood for our nightly enrichment pipeline, but one procurement item has come up with our security and platform teams.

The pipeline submits very large async inference jobs (10k–500k records) that can take many hours depending on downstream IO. Our legal/ops teams want the contract to guarantee job completion within 24 hours, but we can't realistically commit to that for all jobs given variability and backpressure.

Can Redwood provide a carveout / exception for async bulk jobs specifying: 1) a 24–48h completion window for large runs, 2) a bounded retry policy (we prefer retries <=3), and 3) required idempotency keys to avoid double-processing? They also want a remediation metric (service credits) if a job misses the completion window by more than 48 hours.

I've attached a short summary from our SREs (ACME_batch_sla_request_20260210.pdf). Let me know if you prefer a technical call with our platform team.

Best,
Gabe
Sr. Platform Engineer — Acme Analytics

Attachment: ACME_batch_sla_request_20260210.pdf (1 page; summary of ACME async job profiles)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Bulk async SLA needs — completion window flexibility

Hi Gabe —

Thanks for the clear summary and the SRE doc, appreciated. Short answer: yes, we can support a contractual carveout for large async/batch jobs, but we need to define measurable conditions and mitigations. Proposed approach: 

- Scope: carveout applies only to jobs flagged as "bulk_async" in the API (metadata flag) or submitted via our Batch ingestion endpoint.
- Completion window: standard job completion SLA remains 4 hours for normal small/interactive workloads; carveout window for bulk_async = 24–72 hours depending on job size tiers (we propose 24h for <=50k items, 48h for 50–250k, 72h for >250k).
- Retries: recommended client-side retry <=3; Redwood will perform up to 2 worker-level retries for transient infra failures.
- Idempotency: jobs must include idempotency_token (UUID) or a dedupe key; server will store token for 7 days by default (configurable for enterprise).
- Remediation: if completion exceeds upper bound (72h for largest tier), service credit = X% for the affected job run; we can map this to credits on the invoice.

I'll loop in Marcus and Laura to confirm the technical and commercial details and will send a draft carveout clause for your legal team. If that sounds good, let's schedule a 30-min technical sync.

Thanks,
Naomi
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding Gabe's ask from Acme. Key asks: defined completion window for bulk jobs, bounded retry policy, idempotency requirement, and service credits for misses.

Questions for engineering/legal: 
1) Can the runtime expose an explicit job metadata flag (bulk_async) that changes scheduling priority and routing?
2) Storage: how long do we persist idempotency tokens for batch jobs today and what's the cost impact?
3) Retries: is 2 worker-level retries + up to 3 client retries reasonable? Any gotchas with dedupe keys and KV cache?
4) Can we produce a deterministic definition for "job completion" (success/failure/partial-run with N% processed) that legal can accept?

Please comment inline — I want to close commercial language by 2/16 so we can get DocuSign moving.

Thanks,
Naomi

Naomi / Laura —

Technical notes from infra: 
- bulk_async flag: trivial to accept as a job attribute; we will tag and route those jobs to the "batch" queue which has lower scheduling priority but larger concurrency allowance.
- Idempotency tokens: we currently persist job-level idempotency keys for 7 days in our metadata store (configurable up to 30 days for enterprise). Storing for 30 days increases metadata footprint approx +0.6% on large accounts — acceptable.
- Retries: runtime automatically retries transient worker failures twice. Client-side should limit to 3 attempts with exponential backoff. Important: we must enforce idempotency_token semantics so retries are no-ops if token already observed.
- Definition of completion: propose "job completed" = final status = SUCCESS or FAILED with no in-flight tasks; partial success where >=95% items processed will be considered successful for SLA purposes (we will surface error counts in job metadata). This avoids long tails from a tiny subset of problematic records.
- Monitoring/alerts: we can emit per-job completion_time metric; can add alerting thresholds to trigger manual remediation if a job exceeds expected tier window.

I think the 24/48/72 tiering Naomi proposed is reasonable. For service credits, suggest a graduated credit: miss <=24h past upper bound = 10% job credit; >24h past upper bound = 25% credit; requires we define "upper bound" per tier.

I'll attach a short snip of runbook/implementation notes — will copy that into the draft clause.

Marcus
Senior SWE, Serving Runtime

Hi Gabe —

Thanks for your patience while we pulled engineering and legal together. Attached is a short draft clause (proposed_sla_carveout_draft_20260216.docx) that captures what we discussed. Key points: 

- Applicability: Jobs must set job_type=\"bulk_async\" or be submitted via the Batch endpoint to be eligible for the carveout.
- Completion tiers: <=50k items = target 24h / upper bound 24h; 50k–250k = target 36h / upper bound 48h; >250k = target 48h / upper bound 72h. Upper bounds are the contractual limits that map to credits.
- Retries: Redwood performs up to 2 internal retries; clients must provide idempotency_token and should retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff.
- Idempotency & dedupe: Required idempotency_token (UUID) or dedupe_key. Redwood persists tokens for 30 days for enterprise customers by default (configurable).
- Partial success: Any run where >=95% items complete within the applicable upper bound is considered SLA compliant; failures beyond that threshold will count toward credits.
- Credits: Miss <=24h past upper bound = credit equal to 10% of that job's compute charges; miss >24h past upper bound = 25% credit. Credits applied to the next invoice.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm Acme is comfortable with the tier thresholds and the partial-success threshold.
2) If yes, we can plug this clause into the SOW and route for signatures — legal has requested final confirmation by end-of-week 2/20 to meet your go-live target.

If you'd like, we can do a 30-min tech call with Marcus to walk through monitoring, idempotency behavior, and retry guidance.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
